target_name: Horizon-Matched Build Minus Buy with Claims-Coverage Floor
rationale: Internally coherent but essentially a mechanical re-pairing of two already-tested legs, with the gate swapped from a worst-year oancf/at floor to a near-collinear oancf/lct floor, so it is very likely a high-correlation near-duplicate of the gen-7 "Same-Horizon Build Minus Buy with Cash Floor" rather than a substantively new mechanism.

target_name: Intangible Allocation Per Dollar of Business Scale
rationale: A denominator change is a modest edit, but the stated purpose—testing whether the repeated build-minus-buy result is an asset-lightness/capital-intensity artefact rather than an allocation effect—is a legitimate identification test with a clear diagnostic payoff, and the expression matches the hypothesis.

The construction genuinely embeds the earnings condition inside the accumulation in a way no archive leg does and the sign logic is consistent, but it sits close to the well-known R&D-capital-to-assets anomaly and will be highly correlated with the plain TS_SUM(xrd,5)/at leg since most firm-years are profitable, so the incremental content may be small.

target_name: Profit-Funded Knowledge Net of Deal Outlays
rationale: This is the previous proposal spliced onto the archive's already-tested "Net Durable Intangible Capital"/build-minus-buy numerator, so it is an incremental composite whose only new element is the profit indicator, and it imposes an arbitrary unit-for-unit netting of two heterogeneous dollar flows without justification.

target_name: Deal Outlays and Near-Term Debt Against the Equity Cushion
rationale: Dividing by book equity (at − lt) is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis because negative- or near-zero-equity firms—exactly the fragile cases the signal claims to identify—produce large negative or exploding ratios that rank as safest, and 1% winsorisation does not repair the sign flip.

target_name: Build Minus Buy with Industry-Relative Earnings Floor
rationale: A coherent conditional pairing that extends the industry-relative floor to the larger income-statement sample, though the claimed resolution of the moat-versus-industry-composition question is overstated since the outer IND_RANK already removes industry level and only the within-window ordering of the demeaned series adds new information.
